💡 Key Takeaways
  • Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise.
  • In a recent development, emma Hayes, the U.S.
  • Men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – By the time U.S. Soccer confirmed Mauricio Pochettino's departure for Manchester United early Friday morning, the announcement itself was far from a surprise. The press release included the usual formalities – Steve Cherundolo, the U-23 U.S. men's national team head coach, would fill in for the Dec. 13 friendly against Jamaica that falls outside the FIFA international match calendar, and the assurance that the search for Pochettino's USMNT successor would begin shortly. Federation CEO J.T. Batson and COO Dan Helfrich will unsurprisingly lead the search, as will "the soccer leadership team at U.S. Soccer that includes" assistant sporting director Oguchi Onyewu. There was one unique detail tucked into the announcement, though.

In a recent development, emma Hayes, the U.S. women's national team head coach, will also have a say in the matter.

Men's and women's national teams rarely overlap at any given federation, largely because there's little need for a crossover event. They operate on different calendars and in the best case scenarios, each team has dedicated members of staff. Hayes' name-drop as news of Pochettino's exit became official, then, is a unicorn-like sighting, even if U.S. Soccer often champions a spirit of collaboration between all of its national teams. It is uncommon for the head coach of one senior national team to help recruit a counterpart but in U.S. Soccer's case, it makes complete sense.

Hayes' coaching career, which spans two decades and two continents, means her inclusion on the federation's soccer leadership team is an obvious one. She is amongst the most respected soccer minds in the game, which easily makes her one of the most key people on U.S. Soccer's payroll no matter how you look at it. That will be especially true in a hiring process that has to conclude with a compelling follow-up act to Pochettino's splashy arrival two years ago. Her perspective might actually be vital in the process, which only adds to the intrigue of what's next for the USMNT.

"We have an extraordinary gift, which is a women's national team manager who's incredibly insightful, bright mind about the sport, who has a set of personal experiences and relationships that span the club and international game, the men's and women's game, the domestic and international club game, and who also has lived in the shoes of what it's like to be a U.S. national team senior coach," Helfrich told CBS Sports on Thursday. "It is a no-brainer that that mind and that voice has a really prominent seat at the table when we're talking about key moves for the federation.".

Sources indicate that USMNT coaches are rarely style hires; look no further than the list of people to hold the job on a full-time basis this century and the picture paints itself. The only thing Bruce Arena, Bob Bradley, Jurgen Klinsmann, Gregg Berhalter and Pochettino seem to have in common, outside of the job they all once held, is that they were all tasked with some sort of cultural reset depending on the task at hand. That likely will not be the case for Pochettino's successor, though, who will inherit a team with a clear style of play, a healthy mix of veteran players and rising talents and plenty of time on the clock until the next World Cup. The job will be defined in part by continuity, even with the necessary allowance for the new hire to put their unique spin on things.

That's where Hayes' expertise should play a crucial role, and the same goes for Onyewu. Hayes' tactical know-how makes her as qualified as anyone employed by U.S. Soccer to establish the right stylistic profile for the next USMNT coach, especially with the spirit of continuity in mind. Pochettino's track record with the U.S. team was mixed but at its best, his high-intensity, attack-minded approach suited the player pool really well and continues to do so. Hayes, a tactical pragmatist who prioritized attack-minded teams herself with Chelsea and the USWNT, will be more than able to help match candidates to the player pool they will spend the next several years working with. Hayes admitted as much on Wednesday when addressing the topic for the first time.

"I work really closely with J.T. in particular and even more so with Dan as we're growing to develop the American soccer movement and J.T. asked if I would be involved as a technical voice, to be involved with the process and I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men's national team coach," she said. "My role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job, albeit with the women's team, and that I've coached for a number of years and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why and like I said, I feel confident in the group that are being put together. I think it'll be a very thorough process. I think that's the most key part of it and like I said, I feel very embedded in what we're doing with the federation so it doesn't feel unusual to me so, like I've said many times, let's build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that's the important part and let's get it right.".

Sources indicate that that's especially true considering the fact that there are very few slam-dunk candidates to replace Pochettino. Pep Guardiola, months into a sabbatical after a decade with Manchester City, is an obvious target for U.S. Soccer but it is entirely unclear how interested he would be in the vacancy. If he's out of the running, the list of contenders with genuine international appeal dwindles quickly but it does not necessarily mean the list of worthy candidates vanishes with Guardiola. The hiring committee will need to be strategic in that case, both in terms of creating a list of contenders and then narrowing them down over the interview process, Hayes providing an important perspective along the way.

The jobs of the USMNT and the USWNT head coaches are hardly apples-to-apples but even then, one will still have an acute idea of what the other's job entails. There is inherent value in having a coach help in the process of hiring another coach, since they hold such singular positions – they are often treated as the be-all, end-all when it comes to their team's success, fairly or otherwise. She can also speak to the cadence of national teams, which varies greatly from the club game where coaches essentially work with their players every day during a long season.

According to recent reports, "Everyone is aware of the major differences between coaching at the club level and international level, and the main difference is just time on the field and time with your players," Hayes told CBS Sports earlier this year when asked about Pochettino. "Every international coach would love to have more time with their team, but that's not the nature of the international calendar and it's something I know we both had to get used to and are still getting used to … I mentioned a few times that it's almost like we are grandparents. We get to see the players for a week or so and then we send them back to their parents, which is their clubs.".

Recent findings suggest that outside of her tactical expertise, though, Hayes represents U.S. Soccer's ambitious turn in recent years as much as Pochettino does. She was hired because of her reputation as a serial winner at Chelsea, where she won eight league titles and seven cups. She continued the trend in short order with the USWNT – two months after officially starting in the role, she won Olympic gold at the Paris Games in 2024. U.S. Soccer has equally ambitious goals for the men's team, though the timeline will understandably be longer for that program. They continue to target the USMNT's first World Cup quarterfinal appearance since 2002 but in between, they also hope to medal in the Olympics' men's soccer event, which is contested by U-23 teams, for the first time when the Games come to Los Angeles in 2028. More than many at the federation, Hayes has experience with the intangibles it takes to reach those heights and that's exactly why she was hired in the first place. It also reflects what U.S. Soccer's executives are looking for in the next USMNT head coach.

"The most notable characteristic is someone with ambition that matches ours, which is high and so when you have, then, that high shared ambition, then you look for the experience, the talent, the understanding that accompanies that ambition," Helfrich said.

According to recent reports, beyond that, though, Hayes in particular has an idea of what the USMNT job might entail. She is the best of both worlds – she began her coaching career in the U.S. two decades ago and has a deep understanding of the American soccer landscape, but made a name for herself in her native England and can also bring a useful outsider's perspective. There is no perfect equivalent to Hayes waiting for the USMNT job since no coach with experience in the American game has truly broken into the top tiers of the sport just yet, the federation likely to settle for one or the other. Hayes' understanding of both orbits, though, makes her an important guiding force along the way. She might be the only qualified person to answer how much to weigh the insider's perspective with the accomplished outsider's point of view when looking for the next USMNT head coach, in large part because she is the only person who boasts an equal share of it.

Hayes' expertise alone means she will be as valuable a sounding board as any, to the point that it's hard to minimize her ability to offer input down to one or two straightforward things. There is one more thing Hayes might have that no one at U.S. Soccer does – easy access to some of the most notable coaches in the game.

According to recent reports, over the course of her successful 12-year tenure at Chelsea, Hayes became one of the most respected coaches in England. She became the first woman to win the Football Writers Association's Tribute Award in 2024 shortly before leaving England for the U.S., and has earned the praise of many of her counterparts in the men's game along the way. Out of anyone at U.S. Soccer, Hayes might actually have the most compelling list of phone numbers in her contacts. She has said Sir Alex Ferguson, a coaching legend if there ever was one after his storied 27-year tenure at Manchester United, calls her "from time to time." Hayes has been in touch with a handful of her contemporaries over the years, including those who have been on U.S. Soccer's radar at one point or another. In her 2024 book, "A Completely Different Game," Hayes said she heard from Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp after having an emergency hysterectomy because of endometriosis in 2022. The pair "sent me long messages, expressing deeply felt emotions," as did Graham Potter and David Moyes.

Industry observers note that the rolodex is a covetable one, if ex-U.S. Soccer sporting director Matt Crocker can serve as an example. His greatest accomplishments during his three-year spell, which came to an end in April when he took a similar role with the Saudi Arabian Football Federation, were hiring Hayes and Pochettino. He had previously worked with Pochettino at Southampton a decade earlier, which made U.S. Soccer's approach easier when discussions started. Hayes' value exceeds her ability to hand her bosses a phone number but it is unlikely to go unnoticed at U.S. Soccer, who clearly understands the expertise she would bring to the search in a variety of ways.

Former Everton midfielder Leon Osman has praised David Moyes’ enduring legacy in the blue half of Merseyside, insisting the Scotsman’s Glaswegian grit made him the ideal fit the club.

Moyes transformed Everton’s fortunes during an 11-year spell on Merseyside between 2002 and 2013, consistently guiding the Toffees into the top half of the Premier League despite operating on a fraction of the transfer budgets enjoyed by their top-flight rivals.

While Moyes never lifted a major trophy during his tenure - falling just short in the 2009 FA Cup final against Chelsea - Osman believes his former boss’s ability to punch above his weight cements his status as one of the club’s most vital modern figures.

"For the majority of David Moyes' time in charge of Everton, he's probably overachieved in terms of what he's had to spend in the transfer market, so while he might not have had the success Harry Catterick did in terms of silverware, he's been so important for the club," Osman told Betway.

"He's a great fit for Everton, and I think it's that Glaswegian way that adapts particularly well to Liverpool because there's a real understanding of what the people of the city are like and what they want to see from their football team. Everton is the people's club first and foremost, and the fans want to see the team work hard and show that desire to be successful and that's something David Moyes has always instilled in his teams.".

It has been revealed that osman was a central pillar of that Moyes era, making over 400 appearances for his boyhood club after breaking into the senior squad under the manager’s guidance. However, the former England international admitted he initially faced an uphill battle to prove he possessed the physicality required for top-flight football before becoming one of Moyes' most trusted lieutenants.

"He's the man who gave me my shot in the Premier League, so I'll always be thankful to him for that," Osman added. "It did take me a while, though, to convince him I was able and I was ready to play at that level, but once he gave me that chance I think he realised that we had very similar outlooks in terms of style of play and how the game should be played and we had a really great relationship throughout my career.".

Breaking: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging new powers.
  • Industry observers note that under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own.
  • Under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging new powers. The lawmakers in the Bundestag agreed to a reform package on Friday.

Industry observers note that under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own. The range of possible measures is broad, from deleting and manipulating data to disabling entire systems and, if necessary, even destroying physical weapons such as drones that could be deployed against Germany.

Under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations. They will, however, not be allowed to use force against people. An independent oversight board is to be established to monitor the agencies.

Opposition lawmakers specializing in domestic policy warned against granting powers that are too broad.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The president of Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), Holger Münch this week again pointed out that today's hybrid attacks pose a upcoming challenge to the organizations safeguarding the country's security. At his organization's annual meeting in Berlin this week, he mentioned the "hybrid attacks" are challenging the "separation principle," which means that the police conduct investigations while intelligence services gather information. The exchange of data between the two is permitted only under strict conditions.

Münch has long objected to this strict division of responsibilities. He has been calling for expanded powers for the police and closer cooperation with the domestic intelligence agency, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, which is responsible for countering espionage and sabotage.

The separation principle results from lessons learned from the Nazi dictatorship, when the Secret State Police (Gestapo) operated largely outside judicial constraints and served as the regime's central instrument of terror, used to oppress and murder Jews, Sinti and Roma, homosexuals, communists, social democrats and many others. The Allied powers that defeated Nazi Germany in World War II then decided that the police and intelligence services should remain institutionally separate and be granted different powers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Historian Sönke Neitzel of the University of Potsdam considers the separation principle understandable in its historical context. At the BKA's autumn conference, however, he described it as "nonsense" in light of today's threat landscape and said it was no longer necessary in a country that has been a constitutional democracy for decades.

In a recent development, while Neitzel considers the separation principle outdated, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the center-right Christian Social Union (CSU) wants to preserve it in its essential form. In his view, even a more extensive exchange of data does not violate the principle. At the same time, however, he has made clear that he wants to transform the domestically focused Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the BND into "real intelligence services.".

This legislative reform brings Dobrindt a significant step closer to that goal. Parliament approved the interior minister's intends with the votes of the governing coalition of the conservative Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, dobrindt insisted that Germany intends to take an active approach to defending itself against cyberattacks: "Anyone who attacks us in this way must know that we are prepared to strike back. They must know that their digital infrastructure, their server infrastructure, and their software will also be targeted by us.".

Industry observers note that BKA President Holger Münch welcomes Dobrindt's determination and points to the growing threat posed by cyberattacks. The line between criminal and state-sponsored actors is becoming increasingly blurred, he argues. As a result, both intelligence services and law enforcement agencies face the same challenge.

To underscore the scale of the threat as he sees it, Münch cited two statistics: in the first six months of 2026, crime originating from abroad rose by 24% compared with the same period the previous year. What concerns him most is that fewer than 5% of these cases are solved. The BKA chief considers this trend more dangerous than ever: "The state's promise of security can become fragile. Confidence in the ability of its institutions to act effectively and remain steadfast is declining.".

Tech Report: The Review: Hibs thought they had turned the corner, but they've gone straight down another cul-de-sac

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.
  • Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 22 November 2026.

Just when they thought they were beginning to make some progress, along comes another embarrassing setback for Hibs and the decision-makers who have led them into this most trying of seasons.

Before the international break, the impression was that their recently-appointed head coach Marink Reedijk had turned a corner with that Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts at Hampden and a 4-0 win at Pittodrie.

According to recent reports, well, if he did, it has taken them headlong into another cul-de-sac. That’s how it felt at Easter Road yesterday when they were trounced 4-0 by Dundee United and left second-bottom of the Premiership table with more than a third of the season completed.

It made rather a mockery of the club’s social media channels, the profile pages of which proudly trumpet their newfound status as ‘Premier Sports Cup finalists’… with an exclamation mark and a golden trophy emoji thrown in for good measure.

Industry observers note that self-respecting Hibs fans won’t be fooled by the propaganda. Not after a humiliating afternoon on which their much-vaunted anthem, ’Sunshine on Leith’, was belted out by a gleeful away support at Easter Road.

Long before Zac Sapsford’s first-half double and strikes after the interval by Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall, some supporters were digging out their anti-board banners and using a megaphone to voice their frustration with those upstairs.

Malky Mackay is under growing pressure from supporters in his role as Hibs sporting director.

Zac Sapsford scores the first of Dundee United 's four goals against Hibs at Easter Road.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley states that he alone was to blame for their 8-0 thrashing by Hearts.

In a recent development, this is how it works at struggling clubs, where fans need someone to blame. First, they target players. Then they single out the manager. When his replacement proves to be no more effective, they have little option but to turn their guns on the board.

Not that there’s anything wrong with holding the hierarchy to account if they are the common denominator in a lengthy period of under-achievement. There has been little sign of progress at Easter Road since Bournemouth owner Bill Foley sold his Hibs shares back to the Gordon family last year, having suggested that they didn’t listen to his input. Big questions are also being asked of sporting director Malky Mackay who was asked in 2024 to lead and oversee the entire football operation, including recruitment and the appointment of a head coach.

Club legend David Gray had his moments as manager, but in the end, supporters wanted rid. Reedijk may turn out to be the real deal but the early signs are that he is struggling with the squad he has inherited. Too many of them failed to do the basics yesterday.

Unlike Hibs, Jim Goodwin’s Dundee United are a strong side with a clear identity. Not for nothing have they gone eight games without defeat, but they scored all too easily as they racked up their biggest-ever victory at Easter Road.

Industry observers note that hibs’ squad appears to be weak, imbalanced and too full of ill-advised signings for Reedijk to make the kind of impact he would like. The holes in it are such that he recently opted to use Scotland defender Grant Hanley as an emergency centre-forward.

In a recent development, reedijk needs to begin an overhaul of that playing staff in the January window, but how much power will be granted in that process? The Dutch coach has already hinted that he will not be given the final say when it comes to transfers.

Recent findings suggest that the fans are nervous about another rebuild under Mackay and his recruitment staff, whose work in the summer window left a lot to be desired. Jason Kerr was a double-winner with St Johnstone, but he has cut a hapless figure at the back. Midfielder Azeem Abdulai, signed on a three-year contract from Leyton Orient, has made only four appearances, just one from the start. And then there is striker Nathan Lowe, on loan from Stoke City, who is struggling to adapt.

Mackay’s record is under heavy scrutiny. He is to be commended for making a profit of around £6million on striker Kieron Bowie, but why has there been no substantial replacement since the striker’s move to Italy nearly a year ago? Can he really argue that expensive signings such as Thibault Klidje and Ante Suto have been value for money?

A club of Hibs’ size, with those resources, should not be in the relegation zone. Nor should they be struggling so pitifully in their own stadium – they have lost nine of their last ten league games there and haven’t taken three points at home since April.

Which tees up nicely Dundee’s visit to Easter Road on Tuesday, not least because the Tayside club suffered a humiliation of their own this weekend. While Hibs were conceding four, Steven Pressley's side were shipping eight in a hammering by Hearts that has surely inflicted significant psychological damage.

To his great credit, Pressley insisted afterwards that he alone was to blame for his team’s wretched performance. That may have been true on the night, but over an extended period, a club’s fortunes tend to be shaped by decisions off the pitch. As Hibs have been finding out.

NWSL introduces fresh player development rule to incentivize youth investment, aims for further expansion

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway.
  • It has been revealed that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m.
  • According to recent reports, the commissioner introduced the new player development rule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest week on the NWSL calendar is here as the buildup towards the 2026 NWSL Championship is underway. An awards show, countless events, and media days were all on the agenda ahead of Saturday's significant game. That included the annual state of the league by commissioner Jessica Berman on Thursday.

It has been revealed that this year, the commissioner welcomed media to the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., and celebrated record ticket sales, attendance, and future expansion ahead of Saturday night's championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current, live on CBS at 8 p.m. ET. She also announced a few upcoming league rules and future match events.

Here are the new things coming to NWSL:.

According to recent reports, the commissioner introduced the new player development rule. While the league previously submitted paperwork for a potential future second=division league, conversation and planning around that is presently paused with the upcoming 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup and efforts to grow NWSL in other ways.

Industry observers note that "As we grow from 16 to 18 teams in 2028, we know that we have to prioritize the pipeline, not just the pipeline of players, but the pipeline of talent that supports the players in the daily training environment. One of the things that makes the United States so uniquely positioned in the global women's soccer landscape is the depth of that potential pipeline," noted Berman in her opening remarks.

"That's why today we're announcing the NWSL Player Development Rule. It's an vital step in strengthening the pathway to professional soccer for the next generation of players. The rule creates actual incentives for clubs to invest in identifying, developing, and retaining young talent, and it gives the clubs the flexibility to design their programs in the way that makes sense with their sporting philosophies.".

More information and the types of incentives will roll out for clubs as the fresh player development rule goes into effect, but it is another step in future roster-building for clubs now alongside general player signings, transfers, the High Impact Player rule, and the Under-18 mechanism.

Sources indicate that the addition of the rule is paving the way for more support staff and systems in place. The commissioner also announced the fresh NWSL Sporting Executive Program, meant to provide more support for club leadership development. The inaugural set of leadership includes six executives from the league who will participate in the program.

Industry observers note that "Developing the future of the sport is not just limited to the players; it's also about the technical staff who surround those players each and every day ... this is a first-of-its-kind program invested in talent, and it was curated and developed in collaboration with U.S. Soccer and FIFA. This newly introduced year-long initiative will provide sporting executives at our clubs with curated, specialized education, mentorship, and leadership development opportunities tailored around the unique demands of our league and the women's professional game," she said.

The NWSL commissioner then announced the future site of the next NWSL Challenge Cup. The 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup will take place in Austin, Texas, next summer.

Recent findings suggest that the tournament has evolved since its first iteration as a placeholder for the COVID-19-affected season and is now a unique one-off marquee match between top clubs, typically the NWSL Shield titleholders and the NWSL Championship winners. In years where one club wins both, the game is a rematch of the previous NWSL Championship match.

"Following the success of this year's Challenge Cup in Columbus, where we took the event to a neutral site to give an opportunity to introduce the NWSL to a newly introduced community," she noted.

The 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup was between 2025 NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current and 2025 NWSL Championship winners Gotham FC. The 2026 competition was held in Columbus, Ohio. The state will now welcome its first NWSL franchise in 2028 alongside another expansion club in Atlanta.

In a recent development, fans will undoubtedly make the connection and wonder if there is a future where an NWSL club calls Austin home. Currently, there are three NWSL clubs in California and only one in Texas, the Houston Dash.

"We're really excited to create another special experience for our fans and our players while making the NWSL a place that can invite upcoming audiences," Berman noted about heading to Austin.

Sources indicate that commissioner Berman celebrated the league's recent return to the nation's capital for another NWSL Championship. The city hosted the 2022 event and now returns four years later with more attention on the league, the clubs, and its players than ever before.

"Today, we're bigger, stronger, more visible, and more ambitious than ever before, and the next five years are going to redefine what's possible. We have an extraordinary opportunity in front of us, and we intend to seize it," she stated.

It has been revealed that two incoming clubs set for 2028 and latest player roster rules are just the beginning of NWSL's next chapter. There's still the potential for more clubs on the horizon, and current clubs Houston Dash and Racing Louisville are in the process of vetting for a sale to new ownership as franchise entry fees into the league are booming to new heights.

And of course, there is still the biggest game of the year to play on Saturday.

"The Washington Spirit are back in the championship for the third consecutive year, determined to bring home that title. And standing in their way is the Kansas City Current, with its own ambitions to win a championship after winning the Shield in 2025. These are two exceptional clubs, two incredibly passionate fan base, and the championship is still to be decided, [we're] very excited about the rest of this week.".

His club have revealed they are looking to identify those who sent messages to the 26-year-old, whose family were threatened in one of the posts seen by Telegraph Sport after the 1-0 victory.

Leeds say they are “appalled at the disgusting, racist social-media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered” and will push for punishments to be taken.

Sources indicate that the club added in a statement: “Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms. There is no place for racism in football or society.

“The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.

“Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time. Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse.”.

Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, described Bogle as the “softest player” in the Premier League who would never try to hurt an opponent.

Referee John Brooks did not concern a yellow card, with VAR Tony Harrington sticking with the on-field decision.

“I’m confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge,” Harrington was quoted on the major screen at Elland Road.

Tottenham will make a formal complaint to Pro Ref over the decision not to send off Bogle.

“I haven’t watched the scenes back so I can’t give you a clear opinion, out of the game it looked a handball but the scene with Jayden was not too far away from my bench and it looked a very unlucky coming together,” Farke noted.

“Fingers crossed for Mathys that he is back soon, but it looked like there was not much speed in this action, but Jayden Bogle is one of the most fair players in the country, he would never injure or foul a player on purpose because he is such a fair character.”.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. The home side, lions at night and mice in the morning, have the unenviable record of 21 top-flight matches with a kick-off time before 3pm without a win. All that extra TV moolah comes in handy but their home ground, a bearpit under the floodlights, is neutered when its denizens are yawning instead of being fired up by social lubricant.

Daniel Farke’s team started the campaign well but are now without a win in five, drawing three matches with teams beneath them in the table – Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland – and  losing to two above them, Arsenal and Bournemouth. In fairness they played well against the champions for an hour and were deservedly in the lead until Mikel Arteta turnd to his billionaire’s bench and changed the game. At Bournemouth last week they also made a decent start, had a goal disallowed for striking Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s arm and then James Trafford chucked one in.

They never recovered, found themselves increasingly bogged down when trying to unlock a low block and were mugged on the break in added time to lose 2-0. They are a robust side overly reliant on their wing-backs to create chances for their No 9 in the absence of the injured Noah Okafor who was unavailable to train with the team this week because of a groin injury but may be fit enough for the bench.

Spurs, by contrast, are buoyant following three wins on the bounce – over Coventry, Chelsea and Palace, two with clean sheets – that has taken them from 19th to ninth, three places above Leeds. They have won their last three visits to Elland Road, 0-4 under Antonio Conte, which proved to be the last match of Marcelo Bielsa’s glorious spell at the Peacocks, 1-4 under Ryan Mason, which sealed Leeds’ relegation, and 1-2 under Tomas Frank last year by virtue of goals from Mathys Tel and Mohammed Kudus as the home side struggled against their width back in the days before their switch to a back three.

Why Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch face a fight for their Liverpool futures under Andoni Iraola

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1427 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eighteen months ago, on his first return to Merseyside since leaving the club as manager the summer before, Jurgen Klopp spoke at a charity event at Liverpool Cathedral and singled out Dominik Szoboszlai for praise.
  • Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No.
  • Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eighteen months ago, on his first return to Merseyside since leaving the club as manager the summer before, Jurgen Klopp spoke at a charity event at Liverpool Cathedral and singled out Dominik Szoboszlai for praise.

Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No. 10 role as Arne Slot’s side swept to the title.

Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.

“I think, for me, it’s about, in his mind, managing how much he presses and when to go, as opposed to just pressing for pressing’s sake,” Daniel Sturridge explained during Sky Sports' coverage of the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace.

“I’m not saying that he does that all the time, but I think the reason why Liverpool are open is because they don’t have someone who’s reading in front of the defence.”.

According to recent reports, that title-winning campaign two seasons ago saw Szoboszlai vital to everything Liverpool did well, with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch complementing each other - everything was seemingly perfectly balanced. Gravenberch played in a more restricted No. 6 role in front of defence, Mac Allister was the box-to-box No. 8, and Szoboszlai was the all-action, pressing No. 10.

According to recent reports, however, Slot worried that opponents had found out how to play against his team, and perhaps aware of losing Trent Alexander-Arnold’s unique creativity from deep, opted for a changed midfield set up. It actually began in the final away game of the title-winning season, away to Brighton, when Szoboszlai started in a two-man midfield alongside Gravenberch.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that and that’s how Slot continued the following campaign, having signed Florian Wirtz for the No. 10 role. It was a move that immediately had its sceptics. Promising Wirtz the central role, where he had never truly played before, seemed to leave Liverpool far more open in midfield.

Szoboszlai, though, became the first Liverpool midfielder since Steven Gerrard to score and assist 10 or more goals in a single campaign, scoring 13 and assisting 12 in 53 games across all competitions. He was named the Reds’ player of the season.

That, though, doesn’t tell the full story. Some fans were irked by the Hungarian’s manner, especially after a heavy defeat at Manchester City. The match-going supporter noticed how often he slowed play down and often encouraged others to do so. Slot saw it differently, saying: “He is an all-round player, an all-round midfielder, a modern midfielder in my opinion. I think this season he has improved his game on the ball. Off the ball, he is top three, four or five in the world.”.

With two years left to run on his contract, Szoboszlai was rewarded for his form with a latest contract and named one of Iraola’s new vice-captains following the departures of Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah. Szoboszlai’s importance to the club could not have been clearer, and for many he was - and is - regarded as the most likely captain-in-waiting after Virgil van Dijk departs, whether that’s next summer or later.

But 10 league games into the fresh season and it’s clear that Mac Allister is Iraola’s first-choice pick in his midfield two, and there are now growing calls for Trey Nyoni to be the player alongside the Argentine.

It has been revealed that the pairing of Gravenberch and Szoboszlai was woefully exposed on the opening day at Newcastle, with the Dutchman finding himself very much out of favour once Mac Allister was back available after his later return due to the World Cup. But Mac Allister and Szoboszlai together also appears to lack balance, or understanding of when to press in Iraola’s system. “Both of the midfielders, whether it’s Mac Allister or Szoboszlai, have a tendency to vacate that space in front of the defence because of the press the manager wants to do,” Sturridge noted, accurately.

Sources indicate that injury to Szoboszlai during the last international break opened the door for teenager Nyoni's substantial break, including his first league start against Arsenal and his first time starting three consecutive matches. The reviews have been unanimous. The player who was handed his debut by Klopp at 16 has mightily impressed.

Industry observers note that nyoni’s first thought is always to play forward, capable of playing quick, direct passes into the attackers and splitting midfield in doing so. Some supporters see this as a stark contrast to Szoboszlai, who often runs with the ball or slows play and opts for a less positive pass.

According to recent reports, nyoni is also impressing off the ball, adept at tackling and comfortable dropping into the defensive line to start attacks from deep. The youngster explained Iraola’s instructions recently as being “as soon as you get the ball, it’s just play forward.”.

In a recent development, “Trey is very good on the ball, very calm, he reads the situations well,” Iraola praised in pre-season. “We’re forcing him in the work without the ball, in the press, and he is absolutely doing very well. I think the timings of the jumps are very good. He is always confident on the ball so we encourage him.”.

The newly introduced boss is clearly a huge fan of the player, who was the subject of a late £30 million bid from Nottingham Forest in the summer and who fellow teenage prodigy Rio Ngumoha claims “definitely still has another level to go. You guys haven’t even seen him at his top, top level.”.

It has been revealed that on the bench for the Palace game, having started the previous three in a row - including away to Fenerbahce where he bagged his first goal - Nyoni’s involvement in Liverpool's third as sub at Selhurst Park underlined exactly what his strengths are. He read the pass from Tyrick Mitchell inside his own box, intercepting with his left foot, before looking up and immediately playing a quick ball out to Alexander Isak with his right foot that completely split the Palace midfield and started the attack that ended with the Swede pulling the trigger.

Recent findings suggest that two touches was all it took from Nyoni. Technically, it was superb; the vision and execution perfect. It had some supporters making comparisons to Fabinho or Thiago. There is an argument that Nyoni’s passing style gets more from all the forwards, who clearly benefit when they receive the ball promptly, rather than once opposition defences have been able to get back behind the ball.

Liverpool have struggled against so-called low blocks for the past 18 months, since losing the qualities of a certain Alexander-Arnold (and more recently Salah) - Nyoni offers a much-needed solution to the creative dearth.

That, though, leaves a huge question of Szoboszlai - and Gravenberch, with both having signed latest contracts this year.

“When a young player in midfield is playing ahead of them, that causes a problem,” Jamie Carragher expressed last week. “Basically, about where you’ve spent your money. It means you haven’t spent your money well enough.”.

Throw in reports of Liverpool’s interest in Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, whose late move to Chelsea was scuppered on deadline day, and the picture becomes further complicated.

In a recent development, will Nyoni’s emergence as a genuine option lead Liverpool to quell their interest in the Senegalese? And what to be done with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch if so? It can’t be as simple as selling two of the highest earners, but then you also can’t have two of your highest earners on the bench, either. The midfield conundrum could define Iraola’s first season, and it might lead to a high-profile departure or two.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us.
  • In a recent development, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied.
  • The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a new MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

In a recent development, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

The Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

Recent findings suggest that in Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

Industry observers note that the parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an concern in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

According to recent reports, in the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. As long as that's the case, I'm rarely going to bet against the Herons.

Now the playoffs really are getting underway. These are one-off games where the best of the best are going up against each other. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

It has been revealed that okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Participants: Vancouver Whitecaps, Inter MiamiWinners: Inter Miami.

Hey, it's Messi and Muller, just like we're having a top-tier Champions League matchup. It has been a playoff gauntlet, but the more things change, the more they stay the same. Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers are beginning to show how neurons in the brain detect an infection and tailor physiological responses to fight it.Credit: Dr. Chris Henstridge/SPL.

It has been revealed that A viral cold or bacterial infection can leave you feeling miserable, but each infection produces its own mix of symptoms. Now, neuroscientists are discovering that the brain is the conductor of these responses — decoding the type of pathogen that has invaded, accessing memories of past bouts of illness and even mobilizing immune defences at the sight of a sick person.

The findings, many of which are unpublished, were presented on 15 November at the Society for Neuroscience annual meeting in Washington DC, and challenge the established view of what it means to feel unwell. Neuroscientists have long viewed neurological responses to infection as a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation, rather than a strategy tailored to the threat.

“Sickness is actually not a fixed program, although we often talk about it this way,” mentioned Jessica Osterhout, a neurobiologist at the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, who chaired the session.

A bacterial infection and a cold caused by a virus can both result in fever and exhaustion, yet they rarely trigger the same constellation of symptoms. Bacterial infections, for instance, tend to suppress appetite much more sharply than do colds, which made Osterhout and her colleagues wonder how the brain tells various pathogens apart.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

Your brain could be controlling how sick you get — and how you recover.

In unpublished experiments, Osterhout’s team compared mice injected with a bacterial toxin with those given a compound that mimics a viral infection. To see how the brain distinguished between pathogens, the researchers profiled individual cells in circumventricular organs, which are specialized structures with unusually permeable blood vessels that surround brain ventricles.

When the body has an infection, cells in the circumventricular organs switch on sets of immune-related genes and release distinct mixes of chemical signals. Those signals diffuse to nearby neurons and create distinct patterns of activity for different pathogens, allowing the brain to customize its symptom profile depending on the threat.

Rather than acting as conduits that let inflammatory signals pass unchecked from the blood into the wider brain, these structures “may actually interpret them”, Osterhout said.

Sometimes, the brain doesn’t even wait for pathogens to enter the body to rally the immune system1. Andrea Serino, a neuroscientist at Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, studies how the brain maps peripersonal space, which is the area around the body roughly in arm’s reach.

When Serino’s team placed volunteers in virtual reality, they found that threat-monitoring brain regions became active when avatars bearing skin lesions caused by viral or bacterial infections approached, even when the figures were beyond arm’s reach. Just 15 minutes of virtual exposure triggered a surge in frontline immune ‘sentinel’ cells in participants’ blood comparable to that induced by an influenza vaccine. This reaction did not occur when participants saw healthy-looking avatars or ones expressing fear.

These experiments suggest that the immune system uses “the predictive ability of the brain to react before pathogens enter the body”, Serino said.
